name: Edward Nersessian
title: Director, The Helix Center; Clinical Professor of Psychiatry; Training & Supervising Psychoanalyst
bio: Nersessian is a clinical psychiatry professor and psychoanalyst who co-founded the journal Neuropsychoanalysis and co-edited multiple psychoanalytic texts. His research focuses on "reassessing the fundamental tenets of psychoanalytic theory." He previously co-founded the Philoctetes Center and was affiliated with the Paris Institute before establishing the Helix Center. He is a Distinguished Life Member of the American Psychiatric Association and a Corresponding Member of the Societe Psychanalytique de Paris.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Viviane Silvera
title: Artist & Filmmaker
bio: Viviane Silvera is a Telly Award-winning filmmaker and visual artist whose work bridges neuroscience, psychology, and fine art to explore how memory shapes -- and reshapes -- our sense of self. Her acclaimed film See Memory uses over 30,000 hand-painted frames to illustrate trauma's impact on memory and healing through presence and narrative. Her work has been displayed internationally for two decades at venues including Art Basel Miami, Berlin Art Week, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Collections holding her work include Vanderbilt University, the Clinton Presidential Library, and Duke University. She received recognition in Authority Magazine's "Inspirational Women of the Speaking Circuit" series. Born in Hong Kong and raised in Brazil, she holds a BS in Psychology and Political Science from Tufts University and an MFA from the New York Academy of Art.

name: Kenneth T. Kishida
roundtables: The Changing Nature of Free Will

name: Mark Rosin
institution: Pratt Institute of Art and Design
title: Director of Guerilla Science; Assistant Professor of Math & Science
bio: Mark is the Director of Guerilla Science, an award-winning international arts, science and culture organization that creates live events in unusual places, and an assistant professor of Math & Science at the Pratt Institute of Art and Design. He received his PhD in theoretical physics from the University of Cambridge in 2010 and has been creating live experiences for the past decade. He is the 2015 winner of the AAAS Early Career Award for Public Engagement with Science, and a 2017 Ashoka Emerging Innovator.

name: Nacho Arimany
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears II: Embodied Cognition

name: Nils Noren
title: Professional Chef; Director of Hospitality & Development, Chapman Ventures; Co-Founder & Director, Trade & Union
bio: Noren began his culinary career in Sweden as Executive Chef at KB restaurant (Michelin-starred). He relocated to New York to work alongside Marcus Samuelsson at Restaurant Aquavit, where he earned promotions and the establishment received "two Three Star reviews from New York Times, Three 1/2 Stars from NY Post." In 2006, he became VP of Culinary and Pastry Arts at International Culinary Center, expanding programs significantly. Subsequently, he served as VP of Restaurant Development at Marcus Samuelsson Group, conceptualizing and overseeing 25 restaurants. Currently directing hospitality operations for Chapman Ventures and co-founding Trade & Union. He has published an award-winning cookbook, appeared on television programs including Top Chef, and contributes to culinary publications.

name: Patricia Taylor
title: Chair of the Women's International Advisory Council of International House
bio: Dr. Taylor is married to Kenneth Taylor, former Canadian Ambassador to Iran. She accompanied her husband on diplomatic postings to Guatemala City, Detroit, Karachi, London, Tehran, and New York City, conducting research at institutions in each location. In Ottawa, she served as Head of the National Hepatitis Reference Laboratory and Chief of the Virus Diagnostic Services Division. She has held fellowships from the American Association of University Women, Fulbright, and Rockefeller Foundation. She is a Member of the Order of Canada with an honorary Doctor of Laws from St. Francis Xavier University. Her awards include Woman of the Year from the Canadian Women's Club and the Harry Edmonds Award for Lifetime Achievement from International House, NY. Dr. Taylor was a violinist with orchestras at the Universities of Queensland and California, and danced with ballet companies in Australia, Guatemala, and California. She holds a B.Sc. with First Class Honours in bacteriology and a Ph.D. in bacteriology.

name: Regina Pally
title: Co-Founder and Assistant Director, Center for Reflective Parenting
bio: Regina Pally is a psychiatrist and psychoanalyst, in private practice for over 35 years, with a special interest in parents and couples. For 25 years she has studied and written about neuroscience for mental health professionals and the lay public. Most recently she dedicated herself to working in the community to improve the lives of children and their families. In 2008 she founded the Center for Reflective Parenting, whose Mission is to promote healthy child development, by strengthening the relationship bonds that children have with all those who care for them through an emphasis on reflective thinking. The current focus of her writing is Reflective Parenting in relationship to Child Development, Brain Development and the Parent-Child Relationship.

name: Richard Howarth
roundtables: People & Things in Motion: Economics and the Future

name: Yalda Moayedi
roundtables: Touch as the Ur-Sense: From Presence to Poesy

name: Yotam Ophir
title: Assistant Professor, Communication
bio: Dr. Ophir holds a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (2018) and specializes in "media content and effects in the areas of political, science, and health communication." His research employs "computational methods for text mining, network analysis, experiments and surveys." He has authored or co-authored over 30 peer-reviewed papers published in prominent journals including the American Journal of Public Health, Journal of Communication, and Risk Analysis. He directs the Media Effects, Misinformation, and Extremism (MEME) lab and serves as a distinguished fellow at the Annenberg Public Policy Center.
roundtables: Coding and the Human Phenotype: Manipulated Perception? Fakery, Authenticity, and the Birth of NFTs

name: Hans-Guido Wendel
title: Principal Investigator at the Cancer Genetics Laboratory
bio: Dr. Wendel is a Principal Investigator at the Cancer Genetics Laboratory at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center. He trained in medicine in Aachen and Edinburgh and currently holds Associate Member status at the Sloan-Kettering Institute. His research focuses on identifying novel cancer therapies through genetic analysis, with particular emphasis on lymphatic leukemias and lymphomas. He has identified translation -- the process converting messenger RNA into proteins -- as an understudied area in cancer research. His laboratory investigates natural compounds from plants, marine sponges, and corals that target translation processes, seeking to understand their potential clinical applications in cancer treatment.

name: Tristan Perich
title: Composer
bio: Tristan Perich's work is inspired by the aesthetic simplicity of math, physics and code. The WIRE Magazine describes his compositions as "an austere meeting of electronic and organic." 1-Bit Music, his 2004 release on Cantaloupe Music, was the first album ever released as a microchip, programmed to synthesize his electronic composition live. His follow-up release, 1-Bit Symphony, was called "sublime" (New York Press), and the Wall Street Journal said "its oscillations have an intense, hypnotic force and a surprising emotional depth." His latest album, Drift Multiply (Nonesuch, New Amsterdam), for 50 violins and 50 speakers, was described by the New York Times as "a constantly evolving landscape where sounds coalesce and prism, where the violins both pull into focus and blur into a soothing ether." His work coupling 1-bit electronics with traditional forms in both music and visual art has been presented around the world, from Sonar and Ars Electronica to the Museum of Modern Art and bitforms gallery.
roundtables: Striking a Chord: Hearing and Space
Music to Whose Ears II: Embodied Cognition

name: Andrew Rossetti
institution: Mount Sinai Beth Israel Medical Center; University of Barcelona (visiting professor); Montclair State University (faculty); University of Jyvaskyla (doctoral candidate)
title: Clinical Music Psychotherapist; Coordinator of the Multi-Site Music Therapy Program in Radiology Oncology
bio: Andrew Rossetti holds a clinical music psychotherapy role and coordinates multiple music therapy initiatives in hospital radiology oncology settings. He maintains visiting faculty status at the University of Barcelona and teaches at Montclair State University. Currently pursuing doctoral studies in music psychotherapy, he previously earned a Master's degree in Music Therapy from Ramon Llull University in Barcelona and a Bachelor's degree in classical guitar performance. He received a private grant from Augustine Guitar Strings to study classical guitar in Spain. He leads the NYC Regional Arts in Healthcare Group and serves on the International Association for Music & Medicine's Board of Directors. His research and lecturing span Europe, Asia, Canada, and the United States, with particular focus on Environmental Music Therapy and using music psychotherapy to address trauma and cancer-related challenges.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing

name: Emily Adlam
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Is the Universe a Metaverse?

name: Ken Soehner
title: Arthur K. Watson Chief Librarian, Thomas J. Watson Library
bio: Ken Soehner is the Arthur K. Watson Chief Librarian, Thomas J. Watson Library, The Metropolitan Museum of Art. With a collection of more than one million volumes, the libraries at The Metropolitan Museum comprise one of the largest and most encyclopedic collections of research material relating to the history of art. Ken has been at the Met for 22 years. For the past fifteen years he has been Visiting Associate Professor at Pratt School of Library and Information Science, where he teaches classes on Art Librarianship and Museums & Library Research. He holds an M.A. in Art History from Columbia University and an M.S. from the same university's School of Library Service. He is active in the Art Libraries Society of North America, serving as president in 2008-09 and he is a member of the Council at the Grolier Club, this country's oldest society of bibliophiles.
roundtables: The Library as Reality and Metaphor

name: Setsuko Winchester
title: Writer, Ceramicist, & Conceptual Artist; Creator of the Freedom from Fear/Yellow Bowl Project
bio: Winchester is a multidisciplinary artist who transitioned from journalism to visual arts after relocating to Western Massachusetts in 2006. She worked as journalist, editor, and producer at NPR before shifting focus to ceramics. In 2015, she launched the Freedom from Fear/Yellow Bowl Project, combining ceramics and photography to examine American identity and freedom through the lens of Japanese American internment during WWII. The project involved traveling over 16,000 miles to document all ten U.S. concentration camps. Her work has been featured at the FDR Library and Museum and in a 75th Anniversary exhibition commemorating Executive Order 9066.

name: Gerald Hurowitz
roundtables: Panacea or Poison: Placebos and Nocebos in Modern Medicine
How Deep Do We Go? Behavior, Mind, and The 4-Billion-Year History of Life

name: Koshin Paley Ellison
title: Co-Founder of the New York Zen Center for Contemplative Care; MFA, LMSW, DMIN
bio: Rev. Dr. Koshin Paley Ellison established the New York Zen Center for Contemplative Care, which was the first Zen-based organization to offer fully accredited ACPE clinical chaplaincy training in America. The organization delivers contemplative approaches to care through education, direct service, and meditation practice. He serves as academic advisor for Buddhist students in the Master in Pastoral Care and Counseling program at New York Theological Seminary. His work spans education, clinical practice, and public engagement. Over 30,000 annual podcast listeners access his teachings. He delivers keynote presentations at major national conferences including the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization and the Association of Clinical Pastoral Education. His work has received significant media coverage in outlets such as PBS Religion and Ethics Newsweekly, the New York Times, and Los Angeles Times. He co-edited "Awake at the Bedside: Contemplative Teachings on Palliative and End of Life Care" (Wisdom Publications, 2016). His professional credentials include senior Zen monk, Zen teacher, ACPE supervisor, and Jungian psychotherapist.

name: Morgan Stebbins
title: Supervising Analyst; Director of Training
bio: Morgan Stebbins was a supervising analyst, faculty member and Director of Training at the Jungian Psychoanalytic Association in New York, where he also maintains a private practice. He teaches Religious Studies and Hermeneutics at the New York Theological Seminary in the Pastoral Care and Counseling program. He began his Zen training at the San Francisco Zen Center in 1979. He has written on symbol formation, dreams, the role of mindfulness in analysis, the meaning of compulsion, the archetypal relationship of Buddhism and psychology, and the structural parallels between the theories of Jacques Lacan and CG Jung. His main project is to update the material and message of both CG Jung and Zen to be more accessible to the general reader and more integrated with modern research and cultural developments including gender, relationship and language. Recent and upcoming publications include a chapter on gender fluidity and psyche and a chapter on the relationship between mindfulness and alchemical discourse.

name: Steven Wein
institution: New York Psychoanalytic Society and Institute (NYPSI)
title: Supervising Child and Adolescent Analyst; Training and Supervising Analyst
bio: Steven Wein has held several roles at NYPSI since 1993, including Supervising Child and Adolescent Analyst, Training and Supervising Analyst (since 1996), and Associate Dean for Child Analysis (2010-2016). He is a Life Fellow of both the American Psychiatric Association and American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry. At Yale College, he co-authored "The Assessment of Qualitative and Structural Dimensions of Object Relations" with Sidney Blatt, which became standard in psychoanalytic research. After earning his M.D. from New York University School of Medicine and completing psychiatric training, he established a clinical practice focusing on children and adults with learning, developmental, and neurodivergent conditions. He has supervised clinical courses and taught continuous case conferences since 1993 and instructed special topics seminars covering adoption, divorce, race, sexuality, and abuse. He participated twenty years in a multidisciplinary learning disabilities study group and consulted at educational and social agencies. NYPSI awarded him the Charles Brenner Award for Outstanding Contributions to Psychoanalytic Education in 2008.

name: William Grassie
roundtables: Transhumanist Predictions and the Human Predicament
Complexity and Emergence II: Visions of Cosmic Order, from Particles to People

name: Athena Viscusi
title: Psychosocial Care Specialist
bio: Viscusi serves as the Psychosocial Care Specialist, providing support to field workers before, after, and during deployment abroad. As a Mental Health Officer with MSF, she directed programs across Haiti, South Sudan, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Myanmar, and Palestine, overseeing staff and services in displacement camps and treatment centers. Previously, she worked as a community mental health provider in Washington, DC across multiple settings including a refugee center, domestic violence shelter, and gang intervention program. She holds licensure as a Clinical Social Worker in New York and Washington, DC, with degrees from Barnard College and Howard University School of Social Work.

name: Catherine Wikholm
institution: Private practice in Kent, UK (formerly National Health Service/NHS)
title: Clinical Psychologist
bio: Dr. Wikholm holds HCPC registration and BPS Chartered status. She specialises in child, adolescent and young adult mental health and previously served in the NHS. She co-authored The Buddha Pill: Can Meditation Change You?

name: Eva Weil
institution: Sorbonne and University Paris I; Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS); University Paris VII; Societe Psychanalytique de Paris (Paris Psychoanalytical Society)
title: Psychoanalyst and Researcher
bio: Eva Weil is a psychoanalyst and a member of the Paris Psychoanalytical Society. She holds research positions at multiple prestigious French institutions, including the Sorbonne where she works in the program "Identities, International Relations & Civilizations of Europe" (IRICE), and University Paris VII in the "Psychoanalysis & Medicine" team. She directs seminars at the Societe Psychanalytique de Paris focusing on collective trauma and clinical approaches to psychological treatment, as well as seminars at the University Paris I-Sorbonne addressing war traces and reconciliation issues in Europe and globally.

roundtables: Come Out Wherever You Are: In Search of Consciousness

roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Ryan Tellalian
institution: The New School for Social Research
title: Ph.D. Candidate in Clinical Psychology
bio: Ryan holds an MA in Psychology from the same institution, an M.Div. from St. Vladimir's Orthodox Theological Seminary, and a certificate in Armenian Studies from St. Nersess Armenian Seminary. He is a fourth generation Armenian-American, the great-grandson of Genocide victims. His research interests encompass psychology and theology relationships, positive and existential psychology, forensic psychology, and therapeutic applications of binaural beats. He works as an extern at Mount Sinai Beth Israel conducting group therapy, serves as a research clerk at The Forensic Panel, and functions as technical editor for the quarterly Social Research.
roundtables: Trauma and its Aftereffects, Part I: War and Genocide

name: Tayarisha Poe
title: Independent Filmmaker
bio: Tayarisha Poe is a storyteller from West Philadelphia who believes that all stories are inherently multi-sensory and multi-dimensional, and thus should be told that way. She received recognition including selection as one of 25 New Faces by Filmmaker Magazine (2015), the Sundance Institute's Knight Foundation Fellowship (2016), selection for Sundance Screenwriters and Directors Labs (2017), and designation as a 2017 Pew Fellow. Her debut feature film, "SELAH AND THE SPADES," premiered at the 2019 Sundance Film Festival.

name: Alana Quinn
institution: National Academy of Sciences, Washington, D.C.
title: Exhibition and Public Program Organizer; Art Advisor on Issues in Science and Technology journal
bio: Alana Quinn organizes exhibitions and public programs exploring intersections of art, science, and culture at the National Academy of Sciences in Washington, D.C. She has co-organized the popular monthly D.C. Art Science Evening Rendezvous (DASER) salon since its inception in 2011. Quinn curated the NAS' current art exhibition, Steve Miller: Health of the Planet, on view through January 31, 2018. She serves as an art advisor on the science policy journal Issues in Science and Technology. She holds a BFA in photography and media arts from Alfred University, Alfred, NY and an MA in museum studies from Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C.

name: Alina Rubinstein
institution: NYU School of Medicine; Institute for Psychoanalytic Education (IPE), affiliated with New York University Medical Center
title: Clinical Instructor, Department of Psychiatry
bio: Alina Rubinstein is a psychoanalyst in private practice in New York City. She is on the faculty of the Institute for Psychoanalytic Education (IPE), affiliated with the New York University Medical Center, where she is currently co-teaching "Theories of the Self" to psychoanalytic candidates. She also supervises trainees in IPE's Adult Psychotherapy Program and psychiatry residents at NYU Medical Center. Dr. Rubinstein was raised in a family of musicians and has played the piano all her life. She served as a juror for the first four Piano Competitions for Outstanding Amateurs established in 1999 by the Van Cliburn Foundation in Fort Worth, Texas. An avid chamber music participant, she performs in concerts several times a year with other musicians. Seven years ago Dr. Rubinstein also began studying the cello, wishing to explore non-percussive techniques of producing musical sound.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears? Music, Emotion, and Mind

name: Andrea Norton
institution: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center's Music, Stroke Recovery & Neuroimaging Lab
title: Research Collaborator; Music Researcher
bio: Norton is a classically trained vocalist and choral conductor educated at Westminster Choir College in Church Music. She directed a community Renaissance a cappella ensemble and spent six years at New England Conservatory's Research Center for Learning Through Music, where she contributed to curriculum design and assessment frameworks. Since 2002, she has collaborated with neurologist Gottfried Schlaug on investigations examining "music learning on children's brain growth and cognitive development" and studying therapeutic applications including Melodic Intonation Therapy for post-stroke aphasia and autism spectrum disorders. Her research focuses on understanding how music alters neural pathways to enhance therapeutic outcomes.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing

name: Andrew Shum
institution: N/A (formerly Thread Genius / Sotheby's; formerly Spotify; MIT alumnus)
title: Entrepreneur, Software Engineer
bio: Andrew Shum is an entrepreneur with a background in software engineering and artificial intelligence. He was co-founder of Thread Genius, which built computer vision algorithms for retail and e-commerce applications, including visual search and discovery. Thread Genius was acquired by auction house Sotheby's where Andrew focused on expanding the auction business through machine learning technology. His team pioneered efforts to incorporate vision models for understanding consumer taste and price estimation of artwork. Before founding Thread Genius, he was a software engineer at Spotify working on music recommendation problems. Andrew completed his undergraduate studies in Computer Science and Physics at MIT.

name: Anna Ziegler
title: Playwright
bio: Ziegler's theatrical works have been staged at numerous venues including Seattle Repertory Theatre, Cincinnati Playhouse in the Park, and The Magic Theatre. She has earned recognition through awards such as the STAGE Award, Edgerton New Play Prize, and Douglas T. Ward Playwriting Prize. Her professional development includes residencies at prestigious institutions like the Sundance Theatre Lab and O'Neill Playwrights Conference. She holds a BA from Yale and an MFA from NYU/Tisch School of the Arts. Her published works include adaptations of "BFF," "Life Science," and "Photograph 51," along with a screenplay adaptation funded by the Tribeca Film Institute/Sloan Foundation.

name: Beverley Zabriskie
institution: New York's Jungian Psychoanalytic Association (JPA); Associate Editor, Journal of Analytical Psychology (London); Board Member, The Philemon Foundation
title: Jungian Analyst; Founding Faculty Member and Past President of New York's Jungian Psychoanalytic Association
bio: Zabriskie is a Jungian Analyst with extensive scholarly contributions. She has authored approximately 60 publications exploring analytical psychology and synchronicity. Notable works include pieces on "Time and Tao in Synchronicity" and "Psychic Energy and Synchronicity." She contributed the preface to Atom and Archetype: The Pauli-Jung Correspondence (Princeton University Press, 2001) and delivered the 2007 Fay Lectures at Texas A&M on transformation through emotion, spanning mythology to neuroscience.
roundtables: Synchronicity: On the Spectrum of Mind and Matter
Synchronicity and Other Mind Matter Conjectures

name: Caitlin Snow
institution: Private practice in New York City (formerly Assistant Professor of Clinical Psychiatry at New York-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medicine)
title: Geriatric Psychiatrist
bio: Caitlin Snow maintains a geriatric psychiatry private practice in NYC. She earned her MD from Weill Cornell Medicine and completed her General Psychiatry Residency and Geriatric Psychiatry Fellowship at NYPH-WCM. Previously serving as a full-time Assistant Professor of Clinical Psychiatry and Attending Psychiatrist at NYPH-WCM, she also consulted as geriatric psychiatrist for NYC Elder Abuse Center's Queens Enhanced Multidisciplinary Team. Additionally, she holds an Executive MBA from Columbia Business School.

name: Cynthia Pannucci
title: Founder of Art & Science Collaborations, Inc. (ASCI); Professional Artist
bio: Pannucci's educational background encompasses Fine Arts with printmaking as a major focus and art history as a secondary area of study. Her professional artistic practice has spanned printmaking, textiles, mixed-media, photography, and interactive sculpture. Her exhibitions have been displayed at prominent institutions including The American Craft and Cooper-Hewitt museums in New York City. She has received commissions from Citicorp, The Discovery Museum in Bridgeport CT, The Staten Island Children's Museum, and the NYC Metropolitan Transit Authority. In 1988, she established Art & Science Collaborations, Inc., developing pioneering art-science programming including symposia, public panels, exhibitions, and projects that revitalized the "art & technology" movement throughout the 1990s. ASCI organized four international ArtSci Symposia between 1998-2002, after which the organization shifted focus to "art-science." Since 2006, ASCI has conducted annual international competition exhibitions at the New York Hall of Science, featuring science-inspired themes and co-judged by art and science experts. Event partners have included The American Museum of Natural History, the Graduate Center of CUNY, Liberty Science Center, New York Hall of Science, and The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art.

name: Eyal Rozmarin
institution: White Institute; Psychoanalytic Institute of Northern California; Co-Editor of "Relational Perspectives in Psychoanalysis" book series
title: Psychoanalyst & Writer
bio: Eyal Rozmarin holds a Ph.D. and works as a psychoanalyst and writer. His scholarly focus examines the intersection of psychoanalysis and social theory and investigates how psycho-social factors including gender, sexuality, ethnicity, ideology, nationality, and history shape personal identity and attachments. His research emphasizes belonging as a fundamental psychological and social drive. He is originally from Israel-Palestine and currently resides and practices in New York. His forthcoming work is titled "Belonging and its Discontents."

name: Fred Sander
institution: Weill Cornell Department of Psychiatry; New York Psychoanalytic Institute Psychotherapy Program
title: Associate Clinical Professor of Psychiatry
bio: Fred Sander has been teaching and practicing psychoanalysis and family therapy since graduating from Albert Einstein Medical School in 1963. He is currently an Associate Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at the Weill Cornell Department of Psychiatry and on the faculty of the New York Psychoanalytic Institute Psychotherapy Program. A charter member of the American Academy of Family Therapy, he is the author of Individual and Family Therapy: Toward an Integration, and editor of Created in Our Own Images.

name: Harvey Seifter
institution: The Art of Science Learning (NSF-funded); GE's Crotonville Global Leadership Development Center
title: Founder and Director of The Art of Science Learning (AOSL); Innovation and Leadership Instructor
bio: Harvey Seifter is recognized as one of the world's leading authorities on organizational creativity. He founded and directs AOSL, an NSF-funded program integrating arts into STEM education. As Principal Investigator of two NSF grants, he developed the first arts-based STEM innovation curriculum, established innovation incubators nationwide, and conducted research demonstrating causal links between arts-based learning and enhanced creativity, collaboration, and innovation outcomes. At GE's Crotonville, Seifter teaches innovation and helps senior executives improve collaboration, navigate complexity, and drive organizational change. He is a classically trained musician with two decades leading prestigious arts organizations including Orpheus Chamber Orchestra and Circle in the Square Theater on Broadway. Under his leadership, these organizations earned 5 Grammy Awards, 24 Obie and Critics Circle Awards, and a Kennedy Center Award while reaching millions globally. He authored Leadership Ensemble: Lessons in Collaborative Management from the World's Only Conductorless Orchestra and edited special journal issues on arts-based business learning.

name: Nermeen Shaikh
title: Co-Host & News Producer
bio: Nermeen Shaikh is a Co-Host and News Producer at Democracy Now! She is the author of The Present as History published by Columbia University Press. She has a B.A. (Honours) from Queen's University in Canada, and an M.Phil. in politics from Cambridge University. She regularly speaks on issues ranging from contemporary news media and film to politics and literature. She has presented in various venues including the United Nations, TEDx Danubia (Hungary), the Toronto International Film Festival, the American Psychological Association, the New European Literature Festival, among others.

name: Nirav Patel
institution: Rutgers University (Honors College, Rutgers Energy Institute, Rutgers Climate Institute)
title: Research Scholar at the Honors College
bio: Nirav S. Patel is a Research Scholar at the Honors College, where he researches and teaches programs focused on interdisciplinary approaches to human-environment interactions within social-ecological systems. He holds memberships at both the Rutgers Energy Institute and Rutgers Climate Institute, concentrating on coupled natural and human systems. His teaching emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches to UN sustainable development goals through a common mission course. His work prioritizes collective problem solving that contributes to sustainable solutions.

name: Ralph Wharton
institution: Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons; New York Presbyterian Medical Center
title: Professor of Psychiatry; Attending Psychiatrist
bio: Ralph Wharton serves as Professor of Psychiatry at Columbia University College of Physicians & Surgeons, specializing in the clinical use of psychotropic medicines alone and in conjunction with psychotherapy or psychoanalysis. His research on lithium carbonate in affective psychoses was recognized in the American Journal of Psychiatry's 150-year retrospective. He has published extensively on methylphenidate, electrical brain stimulation, and phantom limb pain. Wharton held leadership roles including President of the Society of Practitioners at Columbia Medical Center (Practitioner of the Year, 2010) and President of the American College of Psychoanalysts. He founded and co-directed the Reiner Center for Behavioral Medicine at Presbyterian Hospital for three decades. As a founding member of the International Society for the study of Pain, he co-authored research on pain tolerance among Sherpa guides, published in Science. He serves as a Distinguished Life Fellow of both the American Psychiatric Association and New York Academy of Medicine.

name: Robert Penzer
institution: Weill-Cornell Medical College; New York Psychoanalytic Institute
title: Clinical Assistant Professor of Psychiatry; Associate Director of the Helix Center for Interdisciplinary Investigation
bio: A graduate of Queens College of the City of New York and Harvard Medical School, he completed his residency and fellowship training at New York-Presbyterian/Weill-Cornell Medical College, where he is Clinical Assistant Professor of Psychiatry, and his psychoanalytic training at the New York Psychoanalytic Institute, where he is on the faculty and has served in various teaching and administrative capacities. He maintains a private practice in New York City.

name: W. Craig Tomlinson
institution: Columbia University; Association for Psychoanalytic Medicine (President); Sigmund Freud Archives of the Library of Congress (Board member)
title: Assistant Clinical Professor of Psychiatry
bio: Dr. Tomlinson is a psychoanalyst in private practice and Asst. Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at Columbia University, where he has taught at the Center for Psychoanalytic Theory and Research for over two decades and directs the Freud curriculum. He designs and teaches courses on Freud and psychoanalysis to graduate and undergraduate students at Columbia's Psychoanalytic Studies Program. His scholarly work focuses on Freud, psychoanalytic history, and eighteenth-century German psychology development. He has also translated German-language works on psychoanalysis, art, and music.
